label: Cross-world strong moral supervenience
term: strong moral supervenience in a selected model
definition: Every pair of cases drawn from any two admitted worlds with equal values of the selected nonmoral profile has equal moral status, including cross-world pairs. The same profile therefore cannot change moral value merely across admitted worlds.
note: A stronger conditional than weak supervenience over the identical typed profile. It does not identify a reduction, ground, unique natural-to-moral mapping across rival theories, or exhaustive metaphysical possibility space. Strong-to-weak follows by same-world instantiation; finite controls witness the converse's failure. Independent applicability remains OPEN.
